summary: Psmb4 perturbation in L4-5 IT CTX Glut produced 1,221 downstream DEGs, including increased Psmc6/Psmd4, Ddit3 and Hsph1 and decreased Gria2/Syt1. Published PSMB4 loss impairs proteasome function, and proteasome impairment induces Nrf1-dependent proteasome recovery plus CHOP/DDIT3 integrated stress, predicting the upregulated proteasome/ISR module; the accompanying synaptic-gene decrease was not itself the basis of the flag.

The L2-3 IT CTX Glut pair had only 19 downstream hits, led by decreased Cacnb3 and Kcnj9 with increased Rangap1 and Pkm. Pair-specific searches for PSMB4 loss or proteasome dysfunction linked to Cacnb3/Kcnj9/Syt1 channel or Pkm/Rangap1 responses found no biologically specific bridge.

cell_type: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
summary: Psmb4 perturbation in L2-3 IT ENT/PPP/RSP Glut induced a 338-gene response with increased Psmc6, Ddit3, Hsph1 and Bax and decreased Gria2/Syt1. The documented PSMB4-to-proteasome-defect relationship, Nrf1 proteasome recovery pathway, and proteasome-inhibition CHOP/ISR program predict this positive proteostasis-stress arm, while the synaptic decreases remain a parallel uncaptured module.

cell_type: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
summary: This pair had 51 downstream DEGs, including Psmd4, Psme4 and H2-K1 increases but also Pcbp1/Bex2 increases and Chn1/Homer1 decreases. Literature links PSMB4 loss to proteasome impairment and type-I-IFN induction, but only the small Psmd4/Psme4/H2-K1 subset fits that bridge, so the direction of the full mixed cortical response remains inferential.

The L5 ET CTX Glut pair had just three significant downstream genes: Pkm and Uchl1 increased and Sort1 decreased. Searches for a PSMB4-specific or proteasome-impairment relationship to the coordinated Pkm/Uchl1/Sort1 pattern did not find a target-to-response bridge.

The NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut response had 489 downstream DEGs, with Psmd4, Ddit3 and Hsph1 up and Gria2, Slc17a7 and Syt1 down. PSMB4 loss is documented to impair proteasomes, and the proteasome-defect-to-Nrf1/CHOP chain predicts the upregulated proteasome/ISR module; the glutamatergic synaptic losses were not directly matched in the cited literature.

The CTX-CGE GABA pair had 43 significant downstream genes, dominated by decreases in Erbb4, Pnoc and Syt1, with only a minor Psme4 increase. Searches for PSMB4 or proteasome dysfunction links to the Erbb4/Pnoc/Syt1 interneuron response found no biologically specific bridge, so the isolated Psme4 hit was not treated as the pair-level module.

Psmb4 perturbation in Pvalb Gaba yielded 1,090 downstream DEGs, including increased Psmc6, Psmd4, Psme4, Hsph1 and Ubc. This matches the documented chain from PSMB4 loss to proteasome impairment and Nrf1-dependent proteasome recovery; the concurrent downregulation of Syt1 and other synaptic genes is not explained by the same direct prior relationship.

The Sst Gaba pair showed 402 downstream DEGs, including Psmc6, Psmd4, Ddit3 and Sqstm1 up and Gria2/Syt1 down. Target-specific PSMB4 loss predicts proteasome impairment, and proteasome impairment predicts proteasome recovery plus CHOP/DDIT3 stress induction, agreeing with the upregulated proteostasis/ISR component.

The CNU-MGE GABA response contained 1,142 downstream DEGs, including increased Psme4, Psmc6, Ddit3 and Hmox1 and decreased Syt1/Atp1a3. The published PSMB4 loss to proteasome dysfunction link, combined with Nrf1 recovery and CHOP/ISR induction after proteasome impairment, predicts the positive stress/proteasome arm; synaptic decreases were materially present but less directly documented.

The only eligible downstream effect in CNU-LGE LSX GABA was decreased Syt7. Pair-specific searches for PSMB4 loss or proteasome impairment causing a Syt7-specific decrease in GABAergic neurons found no direct relationship or specific partial bridge.

Psmb4 perturbation in CNU-HYa HY GABA produced 1,127 downstream DEGs, with Psme4/Psmd4, Ddit3 and Hmox1 up and Atp1a3/Gria2 down. A PSMB4 proteasome defect is expected to activate Nrf1-mediated proteasome recovery and CHOP/ISR stress, agreeing with the upregulated module, whereas the ion-channel and synaptic losses are adjacent but not target-specific in the cited work.

The CNU-HYa HY MM Glut pair had 2,098 downstream DEGs, with strong Ddit3, Hsph1, Hmox1 and Psme4 induction alongside Slc17a6/Gria2 decreases. The observed Ddit3/Psme4-positive arm agrees with literature showing PSMB4-dependent proteasome dysfunction and proteasome-impairment activation of Nrf1 proteasome recovery and CHOP/ISR transcription.

Psmb4 perturbation in MH-LH TH Glut produced 370 significant downstream genes, including Psmc6, Psmd4, Psme4 and Hsph1 increases with Atp1a3/Syt1 decreases. The PSMB4 loss to proteasome impairment to Nrf1 recovery chain predicts higher proteasome-pathway transcripts, supporting agreement for that module while not directly accounting for the neuronal gene decreases.

The TH Prkcd/Grin2c Glut response contained 1,102 downstream DEGs, including Psmc4, Psmd4, Ddit3 and Sqstm1 up and Syt1/Slc17a6 down. Literature predicts that PSMB4 loss reduces proteasome activity and secondarily induces Nrf1 proteasome recovery plus CHOP/ISR stress, matching the upregulated proteostasis arm of this mixed response.

The MB Glut response was broad, with 2,489 downstream DEGs and strong Ubc, Psme4, Ddit3 and Hsph1 upregulation together with Slc17a6/Atp1a3 decreases. Published PSMB4 loss causing proteasome defects and proteasome-defect induction of Nrf1 and CHOP/ISR transcription predict the upregulated proteasome-stress arm.

Psmb4 perturbation in MB P MY GABA yielded 1,996 downstream DEGs, including increased Psme4, Ddit3, Hmox1 and Hsph1 and decreased Slc32a1/Syp. The direct PSMB4-to-proteasome-defect evidence and the documented Nrf1/CHOP response to proteasome impairment predict the positive proteostasis/ISR module; GABAergic synaptic decreases remain a distinct module.

The CB GABA response was small but mostly positive, with Psmc6, Psme4 and Sqstm1 among 23 upregulated downstream hits. Increased proteasome-pathway transcripts agree with the chain in which PSMB4 loss impairs proteasome function and proteasome impairment triggers Nrf1-dependent proteasome recovery; the few Atp1a3/Podxl2/Kdm7a decreases were not the basis for the call.
